title: Punctual cutoff for an already mixed sheaf
statement:
Fix the finite field, coefficient field and embedding $\iota$ of
[def-weil-punctual-weights].
Let $\mathcal G$ be a
constructible
$\Qlb$-Weil sheaf on a
separated finite-type
$k_0$-scheme $Y_0$. Assume that for some $u\in\mathbf R$
it is $\iota$-mixed of weights
at most $u$. Let $v\in\mathbf R$, and suppose that at every
closed point $y$ every eigenvalue $\alpha$ of local Frobenius
on $\mathcal G_{\bar y}$ satisfies
$|\iota(\alpha)|\leq q_y^{v/2}$.
Then $\mathcal G$ is $\iota$-mixed of weights at most $v$.

proof.text: By [def-weil-punctual-weights], choose a finite filtration $0=\mathcal G_0\subseteq\cdots\subseteq\mathcal G_m=\mathcal G$ by constructible Weil subsheaves with quotients $\mathcal Q_r=\mathcal G_r/\mathcal G_{r-1}$ punctually pure of weights $u_r\leq u$. Keep zero quotients for now. It suffices to prove $u_r\leq v$ for each nonzero quotient; zero quotients will be assigned the new weight $v$.

source.place: First proof paragraph: take a mixed filtration.

proof.text: Fix a nonzero $\mathcal Q_r$, put $Y=Y_0\times_{k_0}k$ and $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$. The forgetful functor of [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex] is faithful, so the identity of the underlying object of $\mathcal Q_r$ in the constructible heart $\Sh_c(Y,\Qlb)$ [def-weil-constructible-heart] is a nonzero morphism. Since $Y_0$ is separated of finite type over $k_0$ and $\ell\neq p$, [lem-dl-a1-constructible-fibres-exact] applies to exactly this heart. Its geometric coefficient fibres are computed by derived pullback to $s$ followed by the point-fibre functor, and its statement says that a morphism of the heart all of whose geometric fibres are zero is zero. The fibre of the identity is the identity of the fibre. Hence there is a geometric point $\bar x:s\to Y$ with $(\mathcal Q_r)_{\bar x}\neq0$.

source.place: Second proof paragraph: a nonzero quotient has a nonzero geometric fibre (joint conservativity of the fibres in the actual heart).

proof.text: Let $z\in Y$ be the point under $\bar x$, so $\bar x$ gives a field map $\tau:\kappa(z)\to k$ [def-weil-geometric-point], and $\kappa(z)$ contains $k$ through the structure map. Every element of $k$ is algebraic over $\mathbf F_p$, hence so is every element of $\kappa(z)$; thus $\operatorname{trdeg}_k\kappa(z)=0$, and [lem-kun-closed-point-field](a) for $Y/k$ makes $z$ closed with $\kappa(z)$ finite over $k$, so $\kappa(z)=k$ as $k$ is algebraically closed. The image $y$ of $z$ in $Y_0$ has $\kappa(y)\subseteq\kappa(z)=k$ algebraic over $k_0$, so (a) for $Y_0/k_0$ makes $y$ closed with $\kappa(y)/k_0$ finite, and $q_y=\#\kappa(y)\geq2$. The canonical $k$-point $\bar z:s=\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(z)\to Y$ is the geometric point associated with the $k_0$-embedding $\kappa(y)\subseteq\kappa(z)=k$, an admissible choice of $\bar y$ in [def-weil-punctual-weights] and [lem-wf-rational-stalk-exact]. Now $\bar x=\bar z\circ\operatorname{Spec}(\tau)$, and $\tau$ is an injective endomorphism of $k$ carrying each finite subfield into the unique subfield of the same order, hence bijective. Represent $\mathcal Q_r$ by $K$ in $D^b_c(Y,E)$ at a finite stage $E$ [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. The composition isomorphism of [lem-pod-integral-pullback-composition] on integral representatives, rationalized as in [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], gives $L\bar x^*K\cong L\operatorname{Spec}(\tau)^*L\bar z^*K$. If $\operatorname{Fib}_sL\bar z^*K$ were zero, then $L\bar z^*K\cong0$ because $\operatorname{Fib}_s$ is an equivalence [lem-weil-point-fibre-equivalence], so $L\bar x^*K\cong0$ and the fibre at $\bar x$ would vanish. Hence the fibre at $\bar y:=\bar z$, the degree-zero space of this complex, is nonzero.

source.place: Second proof paragraph: the geometric point lies over a closed point of Y_0, and the fibre at the associated geometric point is nonzero.

proof.text: At this closed point $y$, apply [lem-wf-rational-stalk-exact] to each short exact sequence $0\to\mathcal G_{j-1}\to\mathcal G_j\to\mathcal Q_j\to0$. It gives a finite flag of Frobenius-stable subspaces in the finite-dimensional $\Qlb$-space $\mathcal G_{\bar y}$, with graded spaces $(\mathcal Q_j)_{\bar y}$ and induced local Frobenius. Apply the invariant-subspace characteristic-polynomial factorization of [p-linear-filtration] successively: $\det(T-F_y\mid\mathcal G_{\bar y})=\prod_j\det(T-F_y\mid(\mathcal Q_j)_{\bar y})$. Consequently an eigenvalue on $(\mathcal Q_r)_{\bar y}$ is an eigenvalue on $\mathcal G_{\bar y}$ (evaluate the product at that scalar). This uses the current blueprint version of [p-linear-filtration], with $\det(T-F)$, and needs no semisimplicity.

source.place: Third proof paragraph: exact Frobenius-equivariant stalks and characteristic-polynomial factorization.

proof.text: The nonzero space $(\mathcal Q_r)_{\bar y}$ is finite-dimensional by [lem-wf-rational-stalk-exact]. Its coefficient field $\Qlb$ is algebraically closed, so [lem-zl-alg-closed-endomorphism-eigenvalue] supplies an eigenvalue $\alpha$ of its Frobenius. By the preceding step it is also an eigenvalue on $\mathcal G_{\bar y}$. Purity as defined in [def-weil-punctual-weights] and the assumed punctual upper bound therefore give $q_y^{u_r/2}=|\iota(\alpha)|\leq q_y^{v/2}$.

source.place: Third proof paragraph: choose an eigenvalue and compare its pure weight with the assumed bound.

proof.text: Since $q_y\geq2$, one has $\log q_y>0$. Taking real logarithms of the preceding positive-power inequality gives $(u_r/2)\log q_y\leq(v/2)\log q_y$, so dividing by $\log q_y/2>0$ yields $u_r\leq v$. This applies separately to every nonzero quotient. A zero quotient has zero fibres and therefore no eigenvalues, so its punctual purity condition is vacuous for the weight $v$. Retaining the original filtration, give each nonzero quotient its original weight and each zero quotient the weight $v$. All weights are now at most $v$, exactly the mixedness condition of [def-weil-punctual-weights]. If every quotient is zero, the same reassignment works without choosing a point; for the empty filtration there is nothing to reassign.

source.place: Final proof paragraph: monotonicity in the weight and the original mixed filtration, including zero quotients.

proof_origin.place: All four proof paragraphs, made explicit using existing adic-heart and geometric lemmas.
